### 📦 Phase 28: Domain Testing Architecture & Test Layer Migration
- **Status:** 28.1–28.3 scoped; 28.4–28.5 remain unscoped (each will get its own layered breakdown pass closer to when it's picked up). 28.1 is sequenced *ahead of* Phase 27's remaining work (see Phase 27 Sequencing note).
- **Objectives:** Migrate all existing domain tests to use a lightweight, mocked Prisma layer for fast unit testing, while establishing a dedicated real-database integration and E2E testing framework to validate complex multi-domain database constraints and transaction boundary guarantees. Extended scope, priority-ordered: (1) controller/action-layer (`actions.ts`) test coverage — the thin action layer doing session-check + validation + redirect branching is currently untested despite testing.md's edge-case mandate, and it directly wraps the security-sensitive paths in Phase 27 above; (2) hook-level unit tests using `@testing-library/react`'s `renderHook` for every domain hook.
- **Current-state findings (drives the breakdown below):**
  - No Prisma mock exists anywhere (no `__mocks__`, no `vitest-mock-extended`). All 67 `src/domains/**/*.test.ts` files import the real `prisma` singleton from `@/lib/prisma` and run `beforeEach`/`afterEach` create/delete cycles against live Postgres; CI's `test` job only passes because it runs `prisma migrate deploy` first. These are integration tests in unit-test clothing.
  - `architecture.md` §7 ("No Live DB Queries in Unit Tests… MUST completely mock the Prisma client") and `testing.md` §1 ("Database Cleansing Invariant": real-DB `beforeEach` wipe) contradict each other; the codebase follows `testing.md`, violating `architecture.md`.
  - E2E is already mature: 26 `e2e/*.spec.ts` specs against real Postgres via raw-`pg` `global-setup.ts`/`global-teardown.ts`/`dbHelpers.ts`, with a dedicated CI job. The E2E half of the objective is met; the missing tier is **non-browser real-DB integration tests**.
  - `actions.ts` exists in 4 domains (auth, billing, booking, scheduling — 1,077 lines combined); only `auth/actions.test.ts` exists (covers 4 of 9 auth actions); billing, booking and scheduling have none. `directory` has no actions.
  - 21 hooks exist; only 2 are tested (`useSwitchActiveRole.test.ts`, `useSetUpClientProfile.test.ts` — `// @vitest-environment jsdom` + `renderHook` + `vi.mock("@/domains/auth/actions")`), which become the convention for 28.5.
  - No domain has a `queries/` folder yet (reads live under `services/`); out of scope here — Phase 28 does not restructure source folders.

- [x] **28.1: Mocked-Prisma Foundation & Rules Reconciliation**
  - **Design (confirmed):** Mock library is `vitest-mock-extended` (`mockDeep<PrismaClient>()`, typed against `@/generated/prisma/client` — the adapter-based generated client `src/lib/prisma.ts` instantiates), chosen over hand-rolled `vi.fn()` stubs so the mock surface can never drift from the real client's types and no test author has to remember to stub every delegate method. The helper lives at `src/testUtils/prismaMock.ts` and is **opt-in per test file**: importing it registers `vi.mock("@/lib/prisma", () => ({ prisma: prismaMock }))` plus `beforeEach(() => mockReset(prismaMock))`. It is deliberately **not** wired globally in `vitest.setup.ts` — a global mock would silently break the 4 existing `*.stripe-integration.test.ts` files and the future 28.3 integration tier, both of which require the real client, and would let un-migrated real-DB tests "pass" against empty mocks during the 28.2 rollout. The helper also installs a default `prismaMock.$transaction` implementation that invokes interactive-transaction callbacks with `prismaMock` itself (and resolves array-form batches), re-applied after every `mockReset`, so services such as `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount` (callback-form `$transaction`) are unit-testable without per-file boilerplate; individual tests may still override it to simulate a rejected transaction (the exact scenario 27.2's P2002 handling needs). Rules reconciliation: `architecture.md` §7's mocking mandate is scoped explicitly to domain unit tests (`src/domains/**/*.test.ts`, excluding `*.integration.test.ts` / `*.stripe-integration.test.ts`); `testing.md` §1's "Database Cleansing Invariant" is re-scoped to the `*.integration.test.ts` tier introduced in 28.3 (the only tier permitted to write to a DB besides E2E and Stripe integration). Explicitly deferred: the `testing.md` §4 step-order mismatch vs. `ci.yml` (`prisma generate` runs before `migrate deploy` in CI, the reverse of what §4 prescribes) — real but orthogonal, would violate atomic scope here.
  - **Confirmed sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):

    - [x] **28.1.2.1** Domain Service (governance) — reconcile `.claude/rules/architecture.md` §7 and `.claude/rules/testing.md` §1 per the Design above. Docs only, no code.
    - [x] **28.1.2.2** Domain Service (test infra) — add `vitest-mock-extended` devDependency; `src/testUtils/prismaMock.ts` (typed `prismaMock`, opt-in `vi.mock` registration, `beforeEach` `mockReset`, default `$transaction` pass-through re-applied after reset); `src/testUtils/prismaMock.test.ts` sanity suite: stubbed return values flow through a delegate call, state does not leak between tests after reset, callback-form `$transaction` receives the mock, array-form `$transaction` resolves, an overridden `$transaction` rejection propagates. No domain test files migrated (that is 28.2).
    - [x] **28.1.3.1–28.1.6.1** Controller/UI/Hook/View — N/A. Test-infra-and-governance only; reserved explicitly per the vertical-slice requirement rather than silently skipped.

- [x] **28.2: Domain Test Migration to Mocked Prisma**
  - **Design (confirmed):** One PR per domain, ordered smallest → largest so the pattern is proven on a 1-file domain before touching the 32-file one: directory → auth → scheduling → billing → booking. Each migration swaps the real `prisma` import for the 28.1 helper, deletes the `beforeEach`/`afterEach` DB fixture create/delete cycles, and converts assertions from "read the row back from Postgres" to (a) stubbed delegate return values driving the service's branches and (b) `toHaveBeenCalledWith` assertions on the exact `where`/`data` payloads the service sends — the payload assertion is what replaces the lost DB round-trip, so it is mandatory for every write, not optional. Behaviour-preserving: every existing `it(...)` case keeps an equivalent mocked case (no case silently dropped); any case whose *only* value was a real DB behaviour (unique-constraint violation, cascade delete, transaction rollback, `@default`/`@updatedAt` population) is **not** faked with a hand-thrown error — it is listed in that PR's description as a 28.3 integration-tier candidate instead, so coverage moves tiers rather than disappearing. Pure tests that never touched the DB (`hashPassword`/`verifyPassword`, `booking.schema.test.ts`, `scheduling.schema.test.ts`) are left untouched. `*.stripe-integration.test.ts` files are out of scope in every leaf — they intentionally hit real Stripe test-mode + real Postgres and run only under `npm run test:stripe`. Time-dependent services are pinned with `vi.useFakeTimers()`/`vi.setSystemTime()` rather than relying on wall-clock fixture dates. Exit criterion for 28.2 as a whole: `npm run test` passes with `DATABASE_URL` unset/unreachable.

- [x] **28.3: Real-Database Integration Test Tier**
  - **Design (confirmed):** New `*.integration.test.ts` convention (mirrors `*.stripe-integration.test.ts`) with its own `vitest.integration.config.mts` + `test:integration` script + CI job against a `postgres:16` service container, excluded from the main `vitest.config.mts`. Targets only what mocks structurally cannot prove: unique-constraint races (the `ClientProfile` `instagramHandle`/`email` TOCTOU P2002 race 27.2 documents), double-booking / adjacent-slot overflow capping (CLAUDE.md invariant #1) under concurrent writes, `onDelete` cascade/SetNull behaviour, `$transaction` rollback guarantees, plus every candidate handed off by 28.2's migrated tests (see Sequencing note). Fixture isolation: unique-per-test data (`randomUUID`-suffixed handles/emails, `@example.com`) plus a `beforeEach` wipe bounded to tracked ids via `src/testUtils/integrationDb.ts` (not truncate — it races a shared/dev DB; not per-test rollback — it cannot prove commit-time behaviour such as P2002 under concurrent transactions or `$transaction` rollback). Satisfies testing.md §1's Database Cleansing Invariant. Parallelism: `fileParallelism: false` (single shared DB); concurrency is exercised *within* a test via `Promise.allSettled`, asserting outcome invariants (exactly one winner), never ordering. Fixtures: tests own their data through the real `@/lib/prisma` (no `vi.mock`); they do not reuse `e2e/global-setup.ts` (raw-`pg`, E2E-specific `.fixture.json`). Safety guard: the integration setup refuses to run unless `DATABASE_URL` targets localhost/a `*test*` database, so the wipe can never touch a real DB. CI: dedicated `integration-tests` job (no Stripe secrets, so it also runs on fork PRs). Sequencing: 28.2.2.5 has landed, so 28.3.2.5 is unblocked. The 28.2 PR descriptions are not in the repo, so its candidate list was reconstructed from the `integration-tier candidate` header comments in the migrated mocked tests (`grep -rn "integration-tier" src`) plus the 28.2 migration diffs, minus cases already covered by 28.3.2.3/28.3.2.4. 28.3.2.5 is split into two leaves (billing, then booking) to honour one-leaf-one-PR.

Template: `auth/actions.test.ts` (hoisted mocks, one `describe` per action). `getCurrentSession` is called same-module inside `auth/actions.ts`, so auth tests mock `next/headers` cookies + `getSessionWithAccount` via a shared opt-in `src/testUtils/authSessionMock.ts` (`mockSignedIn`/`mockSignedOut`); billing/booking mock `@/domains/auth/actions` cross-module. `redirect()`: spike whether the real `next/navigation` `redirect` runs under vitest and assert with Next's `isRedirectError`/`getURLFromRedirectError`; otherwise `src/testUtils/nextRedirectMock.ts` throws an Error with a digest-faithful `NEXT_REDIRECT;<type>;<url>;<status>;` shape. - [ ] **28.7: Missing Session/Ownership Guards on Controller Actions**
  - **Design (confirmed):** Surfaced by the 28.4 survey: booking's `approveBookingRequest` (no callers, legacy), `declineBookingRequest`, `reviewBookingRequestAction` and `confirmProposedBookingAction` have no session/ownership guard, and every scheduling action takes `artistId` from the client payload with no session guard (validation.md §2). `confirmTimeSlotAction` has no callers but is an exported `"use server"` function, i.e. an unauthenticated slot-write endpoint for any `artistId`; scheduling cannot verify `bookingRequestId` ownership without reading booking tables (architecture.md §1) or importing booking (§4), so it is deleted rather than guarded (`reviewBookingRequestAction` supersedes it; the service-layer `confirmTimeSlot.ts` stays because booking reuses `createBookedTimeSlots`/`isSlotConflict`). `getAvailableSlotsAction` stays intentionally public (the guest booking wizard calls it). Guards live in the controller, matching `rescheduleApprovedBookingAction` and billing: `requireArtistId()` (checks `activeRole`, not `role`) then `requireOwnedRequest()`; a non-artist returns the "signed in as an artist" message, a non-owner/missing request returns `REQUEST_NOT_FOUND_ERROR_MESSAGE` (no enumeration). Ownership is immutable (`BookingRequest.artistId` never changes), so check-then-act cannot race. Scheduling settings actions drop `artistId` from their Zod schemas and derive it from the session; the hooks keep sending a now-ignored `artistId` (Zod strips unknown keys), so no UI/Hook/View change is needed. Each guard leaf creates the domain's `actions.test.ts` with a guard table (signed-out, `activeRole: "CLIENT"`, non-owner, owner; service NOT called on any rejection; hostile `artistId` payload ignored); 28.4.3.4 / 28.4.3.6–28.4.3.8 extend those files and assert guarded behaviour. **Flagged, not fixed:** (1) `approveBookingRequest` is guarded here but should be deleted in a separate follow-up; (2) `setBookingRequestStatus` has no status precondition (declining an already-APPROVED request orphans its BOOKED slots and skips strike logic); (3) the now-ignored `artistId` prop/payload key in `useWeeklyHoursSettings`/`useScheduleOverrides`/`WeeklyHoursSettings`/`BlackoutDateSettings` is dead and should be cleaned up separately; (4) `requireArtistId` is now duplicated in billing, booking and scheduling (architecture.md §4.B shared-logic extraction candidate).

- [x] **28.9: Throwaway Local Test Database** (execute 1.1 → 2.1 → 2.2 → 2.3)
  - Local integration and E2E runs use `.env`'s `DATABASE_URL`, which is the dev database (`localhost:5432/vettr`). `assertSafeDatabaseUrl` accepts any localhost URL, so the integration tier writes to and deletes from the dev DB. E2E `global-setup.ts`/`global-teardown.ts` have no guard at all.
  - CI gets a fresh `postgres:16` service container on 5432 per job. Locally 5432 is taken, so each session (human or agent) improvises its own container.
  - Goal: one command per DB-backed suite that starts a throwaway Postgres, migrates it the way CI does, runs the suite against it and always removes it, leaving `git status` clean.
  - **Design (confirmed 2026-10-11):**
    - A Node wrapper, `scripts/test-db/with-test-db.ts` (run with `tsx`), takes npm script names. No new dependencies: the `docker` CLI plus the existing `pg` and `tsx`.
      - Starts `postgres:16` with CI's credentials and DB name (`postgres`/`postgres`/`vettr_test`), a unique container name, a `vettr.test-db` label, data on tmpfs, and a host port Docker picks on `127.0.0.1`. Parallel runs (worktrees, agents) never collide.
      - Waits for a TCP `SELECT 1`, then runs `prisma generate` and `prisma migrate deploy` (CI's order; never `migrate dev`, so no migration files appear).
      - Runs each `npm run <script>` with `DATABASE_URL` set in the environment. Every `.env` loader here (`dotenv` in the Vitest setups, E2E global setup/teardown and `prisma7.config.ts`; Next's own loader) leaves an existing variable alone, so no `.env.test` file is needed.
      - Removes the container in a `finally` and on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP, and exits with the suite's exit code. `test:db:prune` removes leftovers after a hard kill.
      - `--require-free-port=3000` fails fast for E2E: Playwright's `reuseExistingServer` would otherwise reuse a dev server that talks to the dev DB.
    - Scripts: `test:local` (integration tier only), `test:e2e:local`, `test:e2e:ui:local`, `test:db:prune`. Unit tests already run without a DB (28.2), so `npm run test` is unchanged. The Stripe tier is not wrapped.
    - `ci.yml` is unchanged: service containers already give each job a fresh DB. Parity comes from matching the image, credentials, DB name and command order (`constants.ts` names the `ci.yml` image to keep in sync).
    - 2.3 removes `assertSafeDatabaseUrl`'s localhost exemption once the wrapper is in use, so plain `test:integration`/`test:e2e` refuse the dev DB.

  - `testing.md` §2 requires a full-viewport `toHaveScreenshot()` on every new page, with linux + win32 baselines and zero pixel tolerance. A screenshot can't tell an intended change from a regression, so upkeep grows with pages × platforms × UI churn: removing one fixed icon in 50.2.6.3 invalidates 12 PNGs, and the Phase 50 portal headers would churn the same way.
  - **Design (confirmed 2026-10-14):** three tiers, each catching a different class of bug.
    - **Tier 1, behaviour (every page):** role locators, actions and state assertions (`toBeChecked`, `toHaveURL`, `toHaveClass`). Playwright's actionability checks also fail a click on an element that something else covers.
    - **Tier 2, structure (signed-in portal pages and anything mid-redesign):** `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` checks roles, accessible names and states from the accessibility tree and ignores CSS, so one snapshot covers every OS. It can't see colour, spacing or overlap, which is why tier 1 stays.
    - **Tier 3, pixels (stable, public, brand-critical pages, e.g. `/@handle`, the booking wizard, the portal gate, client sign-in):** `toHaveScreenshot()`, scoped to an element where possible, with dynamic regions masked, a frozen clock (`page.clock`), seeded data, and a content assertion before the capture. Playwright only waits for two identical consecutive frames, so a loading state that holds still can otherwise be captured.
    - **Promotion:** a page moves up to tier 3 once its phase closes and its design is signed off.
    - The 12 existing public baselines are already tier 3 and stay. Public pages have no portal header, so Phase 50 header work won't churn them.
  - Data Gateway / Controller / UI / Hook / View layers: N/A — governance docs only.
  - [x] **28.10.2.1** Domain Service (governance) — rewrite `testing.md` §2's "Headless E2E Check" screenshot mandate as the three tiers, and point Phase 59's testing line in `03-backlog.md` ("Every new UI surface asserts `toHaveScreenshot()` with linux + win32 baselines") at the tier policy. Docs only. `.claude/` is gitignored, so the `testing.md` edit stays local; flag that in the handoff.
  - **Flagged, not scoped** (each needs its own breakdown if wanted): Linux-only baselines generated in the Playwright Docker image, which would drop the `-win32` PNGs and make local runs match CI; element-scoping the 6 existing public screenshots.

### 📦 Phase 53: Vercel Deployment & Production Readiness
- **Status:** 53.1–53.3 scoped; 53.4–53.9 unscoped (pre-launch hardening, each needs its own layered breakdown pass when it's picked up). Domain `vettr.studio` purchased (2026-10-06). Sequencing: 53.1 is cheap and can be slotted in anywhere; 53.2 (test-mode staging) is safe at demo stage; 53.3 (real-money go-live) is no longer blocked by 27.1 (login throttling shipped), but still wants a final pre-launch security review.
- **Structure:** this phase holds three different kinds of item. 53.1–53.2 (deployable build, test-mode staging) are the active runway and wait on no gate. 53.4–53.8 are go-live gates. 53.3 is the launch itself and runs last, after every gate in the list at the top of this file. 53.9 is neither (see its note).
- **Stage order (proposed):** 53.1 deployable build (after 54.1) → 53.2 staging on `staging.vettr.studio` (originally slotted after 54.7 and before 54.8; Phase 54 has since shipped, so staging is next. Sign-in and booking depend on email codes, and real Resend delivery — DKIM/SPF, spam placement, latency against the 1s send timeout — can only be proven on a real domain; staging stays in Stripe test mode, so no money risk) → 53.4–53.9 hardening alongside Phase 56, Phase 58 and the go-live phases in `03-backlog.md` → 53.3 production go-live on the apex `vettr.studio`. Post-launch (unscoped, not yet an item): uptime check on `/` and the cron run, Stripe dashboard webhook-failure alerts.
- **Design (confirmed):** Vercel hosting + **Neon free plan** Postgres (plain Postgres, so it works with the existing `@prisma/adapter-pg`/`pg` stack; scale-to-zero wakes automatically, unlike Supabase's free tier which pauses after 7 days of inactivity and needs a manual restore). Start in a UK/EU region and align the Vercel function region to it. A future US East/West move is expected: a Neon project's region is fixed at creation, so it is a new project + dump/restore, and the runbook (53.1.6.1) must document that path and keep the Vercel function region configurable rather than hardcoded in app code. Runtime `DATABASE_URL` uses Neon's pooled (`-pooler`) connection string; `prisma migrate deploy` uses the direct, non-pooled URL. Migrations stay out of the Vercel build to avoid concurrent-deploy races.

### 📦 Phase 56: Deposit Payment Integrity (pre-go-live)
> Found on 2026-10-07 by checking the deposit flow against the idempotency key → record-the-intent-first → webhook-timeline design. No real money moves until 53.3 (staging stays in Stripe test mode), so nothing here interrupts Phase 54, but every item gates 53.3. Every item is *unscoped* and needs its own 6-layer breakdown pass before any code. Phase 57 (`03-backlog.md`) is the long-term version: an append-only payment event ledger and a fix for the booking ↔ billing dependency.
- **Design constraint (proposed):** new payment state (refund status, dispute records) goes into billing-owned tables keyed by `bookingRequestId`. It must not become new `BookingRequest` columns written through booking's narrow functions, so that Phase 57 builds on this work instead of migrating it.
- **Order:** numeric. 56.1 is a cheap spike that decides which refund events 56.6/56.7 listen for. 56.3 is the Data Gateway prerequisite for 56.4. 56.4 and 56.5 share a root cause (the fixed idempotency key): design them together, ship them as separate items.
- [x] **56.1: Prove Which Stripe Events a Deposit Refund Emits** (execute 3.1 → 2.1)
  - The webhook only handles `refund.updated` with status `succeeded`, but the comments in `refundDeposit.ts` and `confirmDepositRefund.ts` name `charge.refunded`.
  - A card refund that is created already `succeeded` may never emit `refund.updated`. If so, the refund backstop is dead code.
  - Nothing proves delivery today: `depositRefundLifecycle.stripe-integration.test.ts` calls `confirmDepositRefund` directly.
  - Use the Stripe CLI (`stripe listen`) in test mode to record which events fire for an immediate card refund, a pending refund and a failed refund. Subscribe the route to the right events and fix the stale comments.
  - This is the first proof of the refund backstop, so 53.3.1.2's live-money refund is no longer that first proof.
  - **Spike findings (2026-10-09, `stripe listen`, test mode, API `2026-08-26.dahlia`):** every refund emitted `refund.created` with its starting status, plus `charge.refunded`. Then:
    - Immediate (`pm_card_visa`, created `succeeded`): `refund.updated`, still `succeeded`, about 1s later. Its only change was the card's acquirer reference number (ARN) becoming available.
    - Pending (`pm_card_pendingRefund`, created `pending`): `refund.updated` from `pending` to `succeeded` about 2 min later.
    - Failed (`pm_card_refundFail`, created `succeeded`): `refund.updated`, still `succeeded` (ARN now unavailable), about 2 min later, then `refund.failed` from `succeeded` to `failed` 5s after that. No `refund.updated` carried the failure.
    - Every `refund.updated` and `refund.failed` came with a duplicate `charge.refund.updated`. `charge.refunded` fires on creation even for a refund that stays pending or later fails, so it never confirms that money moved.
    - Connect destination charges are untested: the test account has no connected accounts.
  - **Conclusion:** the backstop is not dead code. For an immediate card refund, though, it waits on the ARN update, and how long that takes in live mode is unproven. `refund.created` is the only event that reports an immediate success at once. For 56.6: `pending` → `succeeded` arrives as `refund.updated`; `succeeded` → `failed` arrives only as `refund.failed`, and a stale `refund.updated` (`succeeded`) can arrive after it.
  - **Subscribed events** (for the endpoints 53.2.1.2 and 53.3.1.1 register): `payment_intent.succeeded`, `payment_intent.payment_failed`, `refund.created`, `refund.updated`, `account.updated`. 56.6 adds `refund.failed`.
  - **Flagged, not fixed:** `confirmDepositRefund` treats any `succeeded` refund on the PaymentIntent as a full deposit refund, so a partial refund issued from the Stripe Dashboard reads as fully refunded. The app itself only issues full refunds. Owner: 56.6.
  - **Confirmed sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):
    - [x] **56.1.1.1 / 56.1.4.1–56.1.6.1** Data/UI/Hook/View — N/A.
    - [x] **56.1.3.1** Controller/Action — the webhook route also handles `refund.created` (the same `succeeded`-only body as `refund.updated`), and its header comment lists the subscribed events (+ route unit tests, and a Stripe-tier case that replays a real `refund.created` event through the route for a refund whose local write never happened).
    - [x] **56.1.2.1** Domain Service — comment-only: replace the stale `charge.refunded` in `refundDeposit.ts` and `confirmDepositRefund.ts`, and the `refund.updated` redelivery comment in `depositRefundLifecycle.stripe-integration.test.ts`, with the proven events.
- [x] **56.2: Deposit Paid on a Cancelled or Declined Booking**
  - `confirmDepositPayment` sets `depositPaid` without checking the booking's status.
  - Both cancel paths (`cancelBookingRequest`, `cancelApprovedBookingAsArtist`) only refund when `depositPaid` is already true.
  - So a webhook delayed by an outage (Stripe retries for days), or a payment made from a tab left open after cancelling, leaves a `CANCELLED_*` booking with `depositPaid = true`. Nobody refunds the money.
  - Declining an `APPROVED` booking has the same result (28.7 flagged-not-fixed item 2: `setBookingRequestStatus` has no status check).
  - Design pass: when a payment is confirmed on a non-`APPROVED` booking, record it and issue a full refund. Decide whether cancelling should also cancel an open PaymentIntent.
  - Concurrency: a cancel racing the webhook must produce exactly one refund. The per-booking refund idempotency key already dedupes at Stripe.
  - The new branches need unit tests, plus a real-DB race case in the integration tier.
  - **Design (confirmed 2026-10-09):**
    - No new state. A late payment is recorded on `depositPaid`, and its refund goes through the existing `refundDeposit` (`depositRefunded`/`stripeRefundId`). No new `BookingRequest` columns, so the Phase 56 design constraint holds.
    - Policy by the status the payment lands on: `APPROVED` → mark paid (as today). `CANCELLED_BY_CLIENT`, `CANCELLED_BY_ARTIST`, `DECLINED` → mark paid, then refund in full. `COMPLETED`, `NO_SHOW` (and the unreachable `PENDING`/`AWAITING_SLOT_CONFIRMATION`) → mark paid and log a critical alert with ids only, for manual reconciliation (53.7 routes it). No auto-refund there: on a redelivery, a paid `COMPLETED`/`NO_SHOW` deposit looks the same as one used at checkout or forfeited by a no-show, so a failed refund couldn't be retried safely.
    - Retry: on the three refund statuses, `depositPaid && !depositRefunded` always means a refund is owed, because both cancel paths refund in full. So `confirmDepositPayment` re-attempts the refund on every delivery, including redeliveries of an already-paid event. A failed refund throws (ids only), the webhook route's existing catch answers 500, and Stripe redelivers. No route change.
    - Race: the webhook's `depositPaid` write returns the booking's status from the same update, and each cancel path reads `depositPaid` back from its own status update inside its transaction, not from the read before it. Postgres row locks serialise the two updates, so exactly one side sees the other's write and refunds. The per-booking refund idempotency key and Stripe's full-refund cap back this up.
    - Decline: the server declines only `PENDING` and `AWAITING_SLOT_CONFIRMATION` (the statuses the dashboard offers Decline on), with one conditional update. An `APPROVED` booking is cancelled through `cancelApprovedBookingAsArtist`, which releases its slots and refunds. This closes 28.7 flagged item 2 for decline. `approveBookingRequest` still uses `setBookingRequestStatus`, and its deletion stays 28.7 flagged item 1.
    - Cancelling a booking does not cancel its open PaymentIntent. Refunding the late payment already gets the money right, and PaymentIntent cancellation belongs with 56.4's PaymentIntent lifecycle redesign.
  - **Flagged, not fixed:**
    - `reviewBookingRequest` has no status check, so an artist calling its action directly can re-approve a `DECLINED` or cancelled booking (new slots, deposit payable again). Same family as 56.2/56.10.
    - `confirmProposedBooking` checks status and then updates unconditionally, so a decline that commits between the two is overwritten with `APPROVED`.
    - A cancel-path refund whose Stripe call fails is still only logged (56.7). 56.2 retries it only if Stripe happens to redeliver the payment event.
    - The Stripe fee on a refunded late payment is lost (see the PaymentIntent decision above).
  - **Confirmed sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):
    - [x] **56.2.1.1 / 56.2.4.1–56.2.6.1** Data/UI/Hook/View — N/A. Decline is already shown only on `PENDING`/`AWAITING_SLOT_CONFIRMATION` cards, and its new refusal surfaces through `useRequestActions`' existing error path.
    - [x] **56.2.2.1** Domain Service — booking: `markDepositPaid` returns the booking's status from its own update (+ unit test).
    - [x] **56.2.2.2** Domain Service — booking: `cancelBookingRequest` and `cancelApprovedBookingAsArtist` decide whether to refund from the `depositPaid` that their own status update returns inside the transaction (+ unit tests: a payment confirmed after the pre-read is refunded; an unpaid booking is not).
    - [x] **56.2.2.3** Domain Service — billing: `confirmDepositPayment` applies the status policy above. It refunds on cancelled/declined (including redeliveries while a refund is owed), throws on refund failure, and logs a critical alert on a newly paid `COMPLETED`/`NO_SHOW` (+ unit tests per status and path; integration cases in `booking.deposits-and-strikes.integration.test.ts` with Stripe mocked: a payment after a client cancel ends refunded; a cancel racing the confirmation, for both cancel paths over repeated runs, makes exactly one `refunds.create` per booking with the per-booking key; a late payment on `COMPLETED` is recorded and not refunded).
    - [x] **56.2.2.4** Domain Service — booking: new `declineBookingRequest` service. It runs one conditional update from `DECLINABLE_REQUEST_STATUSES` (`PENDING`, `AWAITING_SLOT_CONFIRMATION`, in `booking/constants.ts`, beside where 56.10's cancel allowlist will go) and returns `REQUEST_ALREADY_RESOLVED_ERROR_MESSAGE` otherwise (+ unit tests; integration case: declining an `APPROVED` booking leaves its status, slots and deposit untouched, and declining a `PENDING` one works).
    - [x] **56.2.3.1** Controller/Action — `declineBookingRequest` delegates to the new service after its 28.7 guards, and `setBookingRequestStatus` narrows to approve-only (+ update `booking/actions.test.ts`: decline mocks the service, asserts its args and passes its result through).

Fixture-only edit forced by the index: `booking.deposits-and-strikes.integration.test.ts` mocks `refunds.create` with a unique id per call instead of a shared `re_it`, because its 56.2 race case refunds 10 bookings in one test.

- [x] **56.4: Stale PaymentIntent After the 24h Idempotency-Key Window**
  - The idempotency key is fixed per booking (`deposit-intent:<bookingRequestId>`), and Stripe only keeps keys for 24h. A visit after 24h creates a second PaymentIntent, and `recordDepositPaymentIntent` overwrites `stripePaymentIntentId`.
  - If the old PaymentIntent is then paid, `confirmDepositPayment` returns not-found. The webhook route ignores that result and answers 200, so Stripe stops retrying and the payment is never recorded. If both PaymentIntents are paid, the client is charged twice.
  - Design pass:
    - Reuse a stored PaymentIntent that is still open instead of creating a new one. Retrieve it, then update the amount, or cancel and recreate it, if the amount changed.
    - Resolve unknown PaymentIntents through the `metadata.bookingRequestId` already set at creation.
    - Treat not-found as a logged critical alert (53.7), not a silent 200.
  - **Design (confirmed 2026-10-10):**
    - At most one payable PaymentIntent per booking: the stored one. `createDepositPaymentIntent` retrieves it and acts on its status, through a `Record` over Stripe's PaymentIntent statuses in `billing/constants.ts` (same idea as 56.2's `DEPOSIT_PAYMENT_ACTION_BY_STATUS`):
      - `requires_payment_method`, `requires_confirmation`, `requires_action`: reuse it if its amount, `on_behalf_of` and `transfer_data.destination` match what would be created now. Otherwise cancel it, then create a new one. Stripe can't change routing on an existing PaymentIntent, so there is no update path.
      - `processing`, `succeeded`, `requires_capture`: refuse with a new "already being processed" message. The webhook records the payment. (`requires_capture` can't happen, since nothing uses manual capture.)
      - `canceled`: create a new one.
    - A PaymentIntent is only replaced after Stripe confirms it's cancelled. Stripe refuses to cancel one that's processing or has succeeded, so two payable PaymentIntents never exist at once.
    - Keys: a new PaymentIntent uses `deposit-intent:<bookingRequestId>:<id of the PaymentIntent it replaces, or "initial">`, and a cancel uses `deposit-intent-cancel:<paymentIntentId>`. Concurrent tabs that replace the same PaymentIntent with the same parameters end up with the same new one.
    - `recordDepositPaymentIntent` becomes a compare-and-set. It writes only while the booking is `APPROVED` and still stores the PaymentIntent the caller replaced (or already stores the new one, for a duplicate request), and it returns whether it wrote.
    - The client secret comes after the commit: `createDepositPaymentIntent` only returns a client secret for a PaymentIntent already committed as the stored id. A lost write returns the generic retryable error and no secret, so the PaymentIntent left behind can't be paid.
      - The client can't confirm without the secret, so `payment_intent.succeeded` can't arrive before the write it depends on, whatever order Stripe delivers events in.
      - This relies on the webhook reading the primary database. If read replicas are added, that lookup stays on the primary.
    - Retrieve and cancel are each wrapped in try/catch (architecture.md §6.1). A failure returns the generic retryable error and logs ids only.
    - Booking cancel paths: after the transaction commits, cancel an unpaid booking's stored PaymentIntent through billing's `cancelDepositPaymentIntent`. This is an optimisation, not the guarantee. The guarantee is 56.2's late-payment refund, which Stripe's webhook retries make durable.
      - If the process dies between the commit and the Stripe call, the PaymentIntent stays open. Only a tab that already has the form open can pay it, because a non-`APPROVED` booking gets no new secret. A payment on it is refunded.
      - The remaining cost is a Stripe fee, and the client sees a charge followed by a refund.
      - Decline needs nothing: PaymentIntents only exist on `APPROVED` bookings.
    - Unmatched `payment_intent.succeeded`: no automatic money movement. Under the rules above, it can only come from state left before 56.4 or a bug. `confirmDepositPayment` logs it (ids only) with the event's `metadata.bookingRequestId`: critical when that metadata is set (a deposit payment that wasn't recorded), a warning when it isn't (not a deposit).
      - The route still answers 200, because a retry can't create a match.
      - To recover by hand: fix the row, then resend the event from the Stripe Dashboard or CLI.
    - Left for 56.5: the create call's own try/catch, handling a failed call in the action and hook, and making the key vary with amount and routing. Until then, a create that reached Stripe but wasn't recorded, followed by a parameter change within 24h, still gets an idempotency error from Stripe.
  - **Flagged, not fixed:**
    - A crash between a booking cancel's commit and its PaymentIntent cancel leaves the PaymentIntent open. 56.2 refunds any payment made on it. A durable sweep for cancelled bookings with an open PaymentIntent would fit 56.7's retry cron.
    - `getPayableDeposits` shows the artist's tier amount and ignores precharge. A flagged client's card therefore shows less than the PaymentIntent charges. A flagged client whose artist has no amount set for that tier never sees the card at all.
  - **Confirmed sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):
    - [x] **56.4.1.1 / 56.4.4.1–56.4.6.1** Data/UI/Hook/View — N/A. No schema change (the stored `stripePaymentIntentId` is already unique, 56.3). The new refusal surfaces through `useDepositPayment`'s existing error path.
    - [x] **56.4.2.1** Domain Service — billing: new `cancelDepositPaymentIntent(paymentIntentId)`. It cancels with the per-PaymentIntent key and returns whether it worked, logging ids only on failure (+ unit tests).
    - [x] **56.4.2.2** Domain Service — booking: `recordDepositPaymentIntent` becomes the compare-and-set above (`updateMany`) and returns whether it wrote.
      - Tests: unit tests, plus an integration case in `booking.deposits-and-strikes.integration.test.ts` (a stale write loses to a newer PaymentIntent, a write on a cancelled booking is refused, and a duplicate write of the same id succeeds).
      - Compile-forced caller edit: `createDepositPaymentIntent` passes the id it read.
    - [x] **56.4.2.3** Domain Service — billing: `createDepositPaymentIntent` reuses, replaces or refuses by status, uses the new keys, and keeps the secret-after-commit rule.
      - Tests: unit tests per status and path, including that a lost write returns no secret.
      - Stripe-tier case in `depositPaymentIntentLifecycle.stripe-integration.test.ts`: a second call reuses the same PaymentIntent, and after the tier amount changes the old one is cancelled and can't be confirmed.
    - [x] **56.4.2.4** Domain Service — booking: `cancelBookingRequest` and `cancelApprovedBookingAsArtist` read `stripePaymentIntentId` back from their status update and cancel an unpaid booking's PaymentIntent after commit.
      - Unit tests: unpaid with a PaymentIntent → cancelled; paid → refunded, not cancelled; no PaymentIntent → neither.
    - [x] **56.4.2.5** Domain Service — billing: `confirmDepositPayment` takes the event's `metadata.bookingRequestId` (optional) and logs an unmatched PaymentIntent as above (+ unit tests).
    - [x] **56.4.3.1** Controller/Action — the webhook route passes `metadata.bookingRequestId` and still answers 200 when no booking matches (+ route unit tests).
- [x] **56.5: Deposit Creation Lockout and Uncaught Stripe Errors**
  - Reusing the fixed key with different parameters makes Stripe reject the call with an idempotency error for up to 24h. The parameters change when the artist edits the tier deposit, when the client is flagged for precharge, or when the artist's Connect `chargesEnabled` flips `on_behalf_of`/`transfer_data`.
  - `stripe.paymentIntents.create` has no try/catch (architecture.md §6.1, §8.B). Nor do `createDepositPaymentIntentAction` or `useDepositPayment`, so the rejection escapes uncaught and the hook's `isLoading` never resets (a stuck spinner).
  - Fix:
    - Make the key vary with the parameters that can change, or reuse the PaymentIntent per 56.4.
    - Wrap the Stripe call and return a generic retryable error, logging ids only.
    - Reset the hook's state on rejection.
  - **Design (confirmed 2026-10-10):**
    - After 56.4, the lockout needs a create that reached Stripe but handed out no secret (a lost response, or a record write that threw or lost), then a parameter change within 24h. The retry reuses `deposit-intent:<bookingRequestId>:<replaced id | "initial">` with new parameters.
    - Key: append the amount in pence and the routing: `deposit-intent:<bookingRequestId>:<replaced id | "initial">:<amount>:<connect account id | "platform">`. These are the only create parameters that change at runtime (tier edit, precharge flag or estimate, Connect `chargesEnabled`). A new runtime parameter must join the key.
      - Same parameters still share a key, so a retry or a concurrent tab gets the same PaymentIntent.
      - Different parameters get different PaymentIntents. 56.4's compare-and-set commits one. The rest never hand out a secret, so they can't be paid.
    - The create call gets its own try/catch (architecture.md §6.1). On failure it returns `DEPOSIT_PAYMENT_INIT_ERROR_MESSAGE` and logs ids only (`stripe_create_failed`, like the retrieve). Whether Stripe made a PaymentIntent is unknown. No secret goes out either way, and a retry with the same parameters replays the same key. This also covers Stripe's 409 for two in-flight requests on one key.
    - The record write gets a separate try/catch (§6.2: the call worked, the local write failed). It logs `record_failed` with the PaymentIntent id and the Prisma code, and returns the same error with no secret. No webhook backstop is needed: without a secret nobody can pay, so `payment_intent.succeeded` can't arrive.
    - Action: a try/catch around the session lookup and the service call returns the same error for anything else (the service's DB reads, the session). It logs the Prisma code only. The client-supplied `bookingRequestId` stays out of the log.
    - Hook: a rejected action call (network, a deploy mid-session) gets the same message, and `isLoading` resets in `finally`.
    - Card: `DepositPaymentCard` drops its `started` flag and renders from the hook's state. Until there's a secret it shows "Pay deposit" (disabled, "Loading…" while in flight), so every error leaves a retry button. Today it shows "Loading payment form…" forever after any error, 56.4's refusal included.
  - **Flagged, not fixed:**
    - A PaymentIntent created but never recorded stays open on Stripe. Nobody can pay it, but nothing cancels it either. 56.4's flagged sweep could find these by `metadata.bookingRequestId`.
    - Stripe saves a 500 on create against its key for 24h. A retry with the same parameters gets the same 500 until the window passes or a parameter changes.
  - **Confirmed sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):
    - [x] **56.5.1.1 / 56.5.4.1** Data/UI — N/A. No schema change. The card is a container (View, per 54.8's split), and no primitive changes.
    - [x] **56.5.2.1** Domain Service — billing: `createDepositPaymentIntent` keys a create by amount and routing as above.
      - Unit tests: the key carries the amount and routing, and a changed amount gets a new key.
      - Stripe-tier case in `depositPaymentIntentLifecycle.stripe-integration.test.ts`: clear the stored id after a create. A retry with the same parameters gets the same PaymentIntent. Clear it again and change the tier amount: the next call creates a new one instead of hitting an idempotency error.

- [x] **56.6: Refund Status Lifecycle (Pending / Failed)** (execute 1.1 → 2.1 → 2.2 → 2.3 → 3.1 → 2.4 → 6.1 → 2.5 → 1.2)
  - `refundDeposit` sets `depositRefunded = true` as soon as `refunds.create` returns, even when the refund is still `pending`. Nothing handles a refund that later fails, so the booking reads as refunded while the client never got the money.
  - Record a refund intent as `PENDING` before calling Stripe (architecture.md §6.2). Move it to `SUCCEEDED`/`FAILED` from the events 56.1 identifies. `depositRefunded` becomes a derived view of that status.
  - Status changes must follow Stripe's event time or a fixed precedence of states, not arrival order. Webhooks are at-least-once and unordered, and this is the first deposit state that can move backwards.
  - Prerequisite for 56.7.
  - **Design (confirmed 2026-10-11):**
    - Storage: a billing-owned `DepositRefund` table, one row per booking (`bookingRequestId @unique`, cascading like `Addon`). It holds the refunded `stripePaymentIntentId`, `stripeRefundId` (`@unique`, null until Stripe answers) and `status` (`PENDING`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`).
      - `BookingRequest.depositRefunded` and `stripeRefundId` move here and are dropped at the end, so refund state lives in one place. This overrides 56.3's "existing columns wait for Phase 57" for these two columns only.
      - The migration backfills a `SUCCEEDED` row for every `depositRefunded = true` booking.
    - Stripe status → ours, through a `Record` over Stripe's refund statuses in `billing/constants.ts` (same idea as 56.4's): `pending`, `requires_action` → `PENDING`; `succeeded` → `SUCCEEDED`; `failed`, `canceled` → `FAILED`. A null or unknown status is logged as a warning and ignored.
    - Ordering: a fixed precedence, not event time. `PENDING < SUCCEEDED < FAILED`. Stripe's refund transitions only move this way (56.1: `succeeded` → `failed`, then a stale `refund.updated` still saying `succeeded`). Event `created` has one-second resolution, and `refundDeposit`'s own write has no event time.
      - One conditional `updateMany` moves the status forward, or keeps it and fills in a missing refund id. It never replaces a different refund id, and it returns whether it wrote.
      - A write that newly reaches `FAILED` logs a critical alert (53.7) with ids and Stripe's `failure_reason` (an enum, not PII). A redelivered `refund.failed` writes nothing, so it alerts once.
    - `refundDeposit`:
      - After its existing checks, it records the intent: it inserts a `PENDING` row if none exists (architecture.md §6.2). A concurrent caller finds the existing row.
      - A row that already has a refund id returns success with no Stripe call. That includes `FAILED`: a refund exists on Stripe, and recovering a failed one is manual (56.11). So `confirmDepositPayment` stops retrying on redeliveries once a refund exists, instead of failing forever.
      - Otherwise it calls `refunds.create` with the per-booking key (as today) plus `metadata.bookingRequestId`.
      - Each step has its own try/catch, logging ids only:
        - The intent insert fails: nothing reached Stripe. It returns `DEPOSIT_REFUND_INIT_ERROR_MESSAGE`.
        - The create fails: the row stays `PENDING` with no refund id, which is what 56.7 retries. It returns the same error.
        - The record write fails: it logs critical with the refund id and the Prisma code, then returns success. The webhook attaches the id.
    - Webhook: `refund.created`, `refund.updated` and the new `refund.failed` all go, whatever their status, to a new billing service, `syncDepositRefundStatus`. It replaces `confirmDepositRefund` and reads only billing's table.
      - A refund whose id is already stored advances that row.
      - Otherwise it fills in the id-less intent row for its PaymentIntent, but only when `metadata.bookingRequestId` names that row's booking. That is the case where `refundDeposit`'s write was lost.
      - Anything else, such as a Dashboard refund (partial or full) or a second refund on the same PaymentIntent, is logged critical with ids only and never recorded. The route still answers 200, because a retry can't create a match. Every Stripe charge on this account is a deposit.
      - This closes 56.1's flagged partial-refund item.
      - Endpoint registration (53.2.1.2, 53.3.1.1) adds `refund.failed`.
    - Reads: billing's new `getDepositRefundStatuses(bookingRequestIds)` returns statuses keyed by booking, like `getPayableDeposits`. The client dashboard composes it next to `getClientBookings`.
      - `ClientBookingCard` shows "Refund pending", "Deposit refunded" or "Contact support".
      - With no refund row it keeps today's "Deposit forfeited"/"Deposit paid".
      - An id-less `PENDING` row (a failed Stripe call that 56.7 will retry) also reads "Refund pending".
    - Transition: until 2.5, `refundDeposit` keeps calling booking's `recordDepositRefund` as a mirror, so the legacy dashboard label keeps working until 6.1 switches it. The webhook service doesn't mirror, so a lost write in that window shows "Deposit paid" on staging until 6.1.
  - **Flagged, not fixed:**
    - A failed intent insert leaves no row, so nothing records the owed refund, and the cancel paths only log it. 56.7's sweep finds only `PENDING` rows with no refund id. It also needs to find paid, cancelled or declined bookings that have no refund row.
    - Recovering a `FAILED` refund is manual until 56.11. A re-refund from the Dashboard is logged as unmatched, and the row stays `FAILED` until someone fixes it by hand.
    - The two cancel paths' comments still name the webhook as the backstop for a failed refund call. 2.5 renames the function they mention, but correcting what the comment claims is 56.7's.
    - "Contact support" has nowhere to point: the app has no support email or page yet. One is needed before 53.3, and 56.11 or 53.7 is the natural owner.
    - The `FAILED` alert is logged after `advanceDepositRefundStatus` commits. A crash between the two loses it, and a redelivered `refund.failed` writes nothing, so nothing alerts again. The row still reads `FAILED` and the client sees "Contact support". A durable alert (an outbox, for example) belongs to 53.7 or Phase 57's ledger.
  - **Confirmed sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):

    - [X] **56.6.2.2** Domain Service — billing: `refundDeposit` records the intent first (new `recordDepositRefundIntent`), sets `metadata.bookingRequestId`, catches each step as above and writes the returned status through 2.1.

- [x] **56.7: Retry Refunds Whose Stripe Call Failed** (execute 1.1 → 2.1 → 2.2 → 2.3 → 2.4 → 2.5 → 3.1 → 3.2 → 6.1)
  - If `stripe.refunds.create` itself fails, no refund exists on Stripe, so no webhook will ever arrive.
  - Both cancel paths only `console.error`. `cancelBookingRequest`'s comment, which says the webhook backstop reconciles this, is wrong for this case.
  - Add a bounded, idempotent retry for refund intents (from 56.6) that are still `PENDING` with no Stripe refund id. The 27.4 session-cleanup cron route and workflow are the precedent.
  - Reuse the per-booking refund idempotency key, so a retry after a lost response can't refund twice.
  - Raise a critical alert after N failed attempts (53.7).
  - **Design (confirmed 2026-10-11):**
    - No orphans: the cancel paths record the refund intent inside their own transaction, so the sweep never has to search for paid, cancelled bookings with no row (56.6's flagged item).
      - Billing exports a transaction-composable `insertDepositRefundIntent(tx, bookingRequestId, stripePaymentIntentId)`: one `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (`createMany` with `skipDuplicates`). `recordDepositRefundIntent` uses it. Booking already passes its transaction to scheduling's `releaseBookedTimeSlots` the same way.
      - `cancelBookingRequest` and `cancelApprovedBookingAsArtist` call it when their status update returns a paid deposit with a PaymentIntent. The cancel and the intent commit together, or neither does.
      - After the commit, `refundDeposit` runs as today, and its own insert finds the row. A crash after the commit, or a failed refund call, leaves an id-less `PENDING` row for the sweep.
      - Late payments need nothing: a failed intent insert in `confirmDepositPayment` throws, the webhook answers 500, and Stripe redelivers.
      - The migration backfills a `PENDING` row for every paid `CANCELLED_BY_CLIENT`, `CANCELLED_BY_ARTIST` or `DECLINED` booking that has a PaymentIntent and no row (staging data only).
    - Sweep: billing's `retryOwedDepositRefunds()` reads only billing's table.
      - Candidates: `PENDING` rows with no refund id, oldest `updatedAt` first, at most 50 per run.
        - A row is skipped until it's 10 minutes old, so the sweep never races the call that created it. This must stay above the longest a server action or webhook can run (300s).
        - After 5 retries, a row is retried at most once a day. That also outlasts Stripe's 24h key window, which replays a saved Stripe 500.
        - The cutoffs come from the Node clock (Prisma's `@updatedAt` does too), computed once per run.
      - Per row, in turn, each in its own try/catch:
        1. Reconcile first: list the PaymentIntent's refunds on Stripe. A refund whose `metadata.bookingRequestId` names this booking goes through `syncDepositRefundStatus` (the webhook's own path), and nothing is created. This covers a refund that exists but whose id never reached us (a lost response or a failed status write, with no webhook). After the 24h key window, a new create would get `charge_already_refunded`, and if that hidden refund had failed, it would bypass 56.6's manual recovery rule.
        2. A failed list call skips the row this run. The sweep never creates a refund without checking first.
        3. Otherwise `refundDeposit(bookingRequestId)`, with the per-booking idempotency key and the PaymentIntent stored on the row.
        4. Any result other than success or the generic retryable error (the booking is missing, unpaid or has no PaymentIntent, none of which can happen today) is logged critical, ids only.
      - After each row, `recordDepositRefundRetry` counts the visit: one conditional `updateManyAndReturn` that increments `retryAttempts` only while the row is still `PENDING` with no refund id. A row that got its id isn't counted. The increment also bumps `updatedAt`, so failing rows take turns.
      - The increment that returns exactly 5 logs critical (`refund_retry_failing`, ids only, 53.7 routes it). The update is atomic, so it alerts once. Retries continue daily after that, and the client still sees "Refund pending".
      - Budget: no new row starts after 60s, and the rest wait for the next run. The route sets `maxDuration = 300`, because one Stripe call with stripe-node's own retries can take minutes.
      - Returns `{ reconciled, refunded, failed, deferred }`.
    - Route: `POST /api/cron/deposit-refund-retry`, copying session-cleanup.
      - The bearer check moves to `src/lib/cronAuth.ts` (`isAuthorizedCronRequest`), and both routes use it.
      - 200 with the counts and `durationMs`. A sweep that throws (its read fails) answers a generic 500, so the job fails visibly. Per-row failures are logged and still answer 200.
    - Workflow: `.github/workflows/deposit-refund-retry.yml`, hourly at minute 17 plus `workflow_dispatch`, with the same `APP_URL`/`CRON_SECRET` secrets.
      - curl has no retries (the next hourly run is the retry) and `--max-time 330`, above the route's `maxDuration`, so two sweeps never overlap and double-count retries.
      - An overlap would still be money-safe: the per-booking key and reconcile-first stop a second refund.
    - Both cancel paths' comments say the sweep, not the webhook, retries a failed refund call. Their plain-string refund logs become structured, ids-only logs.
  - **Flagged, not fixed:**
    - A late payment's refund intent is only as durable as Stripe's redeliveries (about 3 days in live mode). If `confirmDepositPayment`'s insert fails on every one, nothing records the owed refund.
    - `refundDeposit` reads the booking outside any try/catch. A DB error there makes a cancel path throw after its commit, so the client sees an error for a cancel that went through. The sweep still refunds it.
    - `refundDeposit` has no status check, and the sweep calls it hours later. A booking re-approved through 56.2's flagged `reviewBookingRequest` hole would still be refunded. 56.10 decides whether `refundDeposit` refuses non-refund statuses.
    - A Stripe 500 on the first create is saved against the per-booking key for 24h (56.5's flag). Retries inside that window replay it, so the alert fires before the daily backoff gets a fresh result.
    - A Dashboard refund has no metadata, so it's never reconciled, and the create gets `charge_already_refunded`. The row retries daily and has already alerted. Recovery is manual (56.11).
    - The new workflow fails every run until 53.2.1.3 adds `APP_URL` and `CRON_SECRET`, like session-cleanup.
    - The 56.4/56.5 PaymentIntent sweeps (open PaymentIntents on cancelled bookings, created-but-unrecorded ones) stay out of 56.7. They aren't refunds, and 56.2 refunds any payment made on them.
  - **Confirmed sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):

    - [x] **56.7.1.1** Data Gateway — `DepositRefund.retryAttempts Int @default(0)` and `@@index([status, updatedAt])` + migration with the backfill above. No app code.
    - [x] **56.7.2.1** Domain Service — billing: new transaction-composable `insertDepositRefundIntent(tx, …)`, which `recordDepositRefundIntent` uses (+ unit tests).
    - [x] **56.7.2.2** Domain Service — booking: both cancel paths insert the intent inside their transaction, and their comments and refund logs change as above.
      - Unit tests: a paid booking inserts with the transaction client; an unpaid one doesn't.

    - [x] **56.7.2.4** Domain Service — billing: new `recordDepositRefundRetry` (the conditional increment and the alert at 5).
      - Unit tests.
      - `billing.integration.test.ts` cases: a row with a refund id isn't counted; concurrent increments alert exactly once.
    - [x] **56.7.2.5** Domain Service — billing: new `retryOwedDepositRefunds` and its constants.
      - Unit tests: the candidate query and backoff, reconcile-first, a failed list call skips the create, a refund, a refusal logged critical, a row that throws doesn't stop the batch, the budget defers.

    - [x] **56.7.6.1** View & Route — `.github/workflows/deposit-refund-retry.yml` as above (the 27.4.6.1 analog).
- [ ] **56.8: Disputes and Failed Payments** (execute 1.1 → 2.1 → 3.1 → 3.2)
  - The webhook ignores `charge.dispute.*` events entirely. A chargeback on a deposit would go unnoticed: Stripe debits the platform for disputes on destination charges, and evidence has a deadline.
  - `payment_intent.payment_failed` is only logged.
  - Minimum for go-live: record dispute events against the booking and raise a critical alert (53.7).
  - Artist-facing dispute UI and evidence submission are out of scope. Decide whether an open dispute blocks further deposit actions on that booking.
  - Design constraint: no new billing → booking calls. Dispute state goes in a billing-owned table keyed by `bookingRequestId` (the Phase 56 design constraint above), and billing must not call booking services to record it. Each new call adds to the circular dependency Phase 57 (`03-backlog.md`) has to undo.
  - **Stripe facts (docs, 2026-10-14):**
    - A refund is refused while a chargeback is open, and after one is lost (`charge_disputed` / `refund_disputed_payment`). An inquiry (`warning_*`) can still be refunded, which closes it.
    - Statuses move both ways: an inquiry can escalate to a chargeback, and a loss can become a late win. One payment can have more than one dispute.
    - A destination charge's dispute debits the platform's balance, and Stripe doesn't reverse the transfer.
    - A Dispute carries its PaymentIntent's id, not its metadata.
  - **Design (confirmed 2026-10-14):**
    - No in-app block. Stripe already refuses the refunds that a dispute rules out, and a paid deposit can't get a new PaymentIntent (56.4). Nothing else in the deposit flow needs to stop.
    - Storage: a billing-owned `DepositDispute`, one row per Stripe dispute.
      - Fields: `stripeDisputeId @unique`, `stripePaymentIntentId`, `status`, `reason` (Stripe's code, not PII), `amount` (pence, Stripe's disputed amount, which can differ from the deposit), `evidenceDueBy` (nullable), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`.
      - `bookingRequestId` is an FK with `onDelete: Cascade` (like `DepositRefund`) and a plain index, not unique.
      - `DepositDisputeStatus` maps Stripe's eight statuses 1:1. No backfill.
    - Linking to the booking: billing retrieves the dispute with `expand: ["payment_intent"]` and reads the PaymentIntent's `metadata.bookingRequestId`.
      - This is the one exception to "metadata never picks a booking". A dispute record moves no money, and the metadata names the booking the PaymentIntent was created for, even one the booking no longer stores.
      - No booking call: the only complete PaymentIntent → booking lookup is booking's.
    - Ordering: every event re-reads the dispute from Stripe and writes its current status. A fixed precedence like 56.6's can't hold, because statuses move both ways.
      - `DEPOSIT_DISPUTE_STATUSES_REPLACEABLE` stops a stale concurrent handler from re-opening a closed dispute. An open status replaces only open ones. A closed one (`WON`, `LOST`, `PREVENTED`, `WARNING_CLOSED`) replaces any other, so a late win lands.
    - `syncDepositDispute(stripeDisputeId)` reads and writes only billing's tables. In turn:
      1. Retrieve, in its own try/catch. A failure logs a `dispute_retrieve_failed` warning (ids only) and throws, so the route answers 500 and Stripe redelivers.
      2. No expanded PaymentIntent, or no metadata: critical `dispute_unmatched` with ids, status, reason, amount and due date. Returns `UNMATCHED`, and the route answers 200 because a retry can't create a match.
      3. An unknown status is logged critical with the raw value, and nothing is written (`UNKNOWN_STATUS`).
      4. Read the booking's `DepositRefund` status, before the insert so a failed read can't swallow the alert. A `due_by` of null or 0 is stored as null.
      5. `createMany` with `skipDuplicates` on `stripeDisputeId`. An insert logs critical `dispute_opened` with ids, status, reason, amount, `evidenceDueBy`, `isChargeRefundable` and the refund status, so a dispute on an already-refunded deposit stands out (the refund is the evidence). Returns `RECORDED`.
         - A P2003 (the metadata names a missing booking) is caught: critical `dispute_unmatched` with its `errorCode`, then `UNMATCHED`. Any other database error propagates (500, redelivery).
      6. No insert: one `updateManyAndReturn` where the stored status is replaceable, writing status, reason, amount and due date. A returned row logs `dispute_status_changed`, critical for `NEEDS_RESPONSE`, `WARNING_NEEDS_RESPONSE` and `LOST` and a warning otherwise (`UPDATED`). Nothing returned is `UNCHANGED`. So each transition alerts once, and a redelivery writes nothing.
      - Ids and enum codes only. Never log the dispute or the PaymentIntent: the expanded PaymentIntent holds `receipt_email` and `shipping`, and a dispute's evidence can hold the client's name and email.
    - Route: `charge.dispute.created`, `.updated`, `.closed`, `.funds_withdrawn` and `.funds_reinstated` all go to `syncDepositDispute(event.data.object.id)`. The outcome is ignored, and a throw answers 500. Endpoint registration (53.2.1.2, 53.3.1.1) adds all five.
    - `payment_intent.payment_failed` stays stateless. The PaymentIntent returns to `requires_payment_method`, 56.4 reuses it, and the Payment Element shows the error inline.
      - The log becomes structured: `operation: "stripeWebhook"`, `reason: "deposit_payment_failed"`, `severity: "warning"`, `paymentIntentId`, `bookingRequestId` (metadata, log-only), and `last_payment_error`'s `code` and `decline_code`.
      - Never its `message` or the payment method. The stale "No failure-handling UI yet" comment goes.
  - **Flagged, not fixed:**
    - A cancel during an open chargeback leaves an id-less `PENDING` refund row. The sweep retries it daily and alerts `refund_retry_failing` at 5. A win lets a later retry refund the client, which is right because they cancelled. A loss fails every day until someone clears it, so 56.11 needs a "settled by chargeback" outcome.
    - Recovering a disputed amount from the artist (a transfer reversal) is 56.12's.
    - A lost dispute doesn't count toward client flagging (CLAUDE.md constraint 4). That's a product decision.
    - Alerts are logged after the commit, so a crash between the two loses one (same as 56.6's `FAILED` item; 53.7 or Phase 57). If the retrieve fails on every redelivery, nothing is recorded, and Stripe's own dispute email is the backstop.
    - A stale open status can overwrite a newer open one and raise a false alert. The next event corrects it, since every dispute ends with `charge.dispute.closed`. A deadline change without a status change isn't written; the Dashboard is the source of truth.
    - CI's Stripe-tier tests share the test account with staging, so each run's test dispute reaches staging as a critical `dispute_unmatched`, as `refund_unmatched` already does (53.7).
    - The route's catch-all logs the raw error object (`route.ts:102`).
  - **Confirmed sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):
    - [ ] **56.8.4.1 / 56.8.5.1 / 56.8.6.1** UI/Hook/View — N/A. Dispute UI is out of scope and the client's refund label is unchanged. API-only, so no E2E (as 56.6.3.1).
    - [ ] **56.8.1.1** Data Gateway — `DepositDispute` + `DepositDisputeStatus` + the `BookingRequest` back-relation (the "billing owns it" comment) + migration in the style of `20261011013021_add_deposit_refund`, with no backfill. No app code. Integration `wipe()` needs no change (it cascades).
    - [ ] **56.8.2.1** Domain Service — billing: the Stripe-status union and outcome type, the three `Record`s (status map, replaceable, severity) and `syncDepositDispute`.
      - Unit tests per path: the retrieve throws, no PaymentIntent or metadata, unknown status, an insert with the exact alert, P2003, a transition with its severity, no transition, and a `due_by` of 0.
      - `billing.integration.test.ts` cases (Stripe mocked): concurrent first syncs make one row and one alert; a transition writes and alerts once and a redelivery is `UNCHANGED`; an open status after a closed one writes nothing; a late win is written; a missing booking is `UNMATCHED` with no row (proves the adapter's P2003); two disputes on one PaymentIntent make two rows.
      - New `depositDisputeLifecycle.stripe-integration.test.ts`, paying with `pm_card_createDispute`: the sync records `NEEDS_RESPONSE`/`fraudulent` and a second one is `UNCHANGED`. `refunds.create` rejects while the dispute is open; after `disputes.close` the sync moves it to `LOST` and `refunds.create` still rejects (proves the no-block decision).
    - [ ] **56.8.3.1** Controller/Action — the webhook route sends the five dispute events to `syncDepositDispute`, and its header lists them.
      - Route unit tests: each event type calls it once with the dispute id and answers 200; `UNMATCHED` answers 200; a throw answers 500.
      - Stripe-tier replay of a real `charge.dispute.created` through the route (as 56.1.3.1).
    - [ ] **56.8.3.2** Controller/Action — the structured `payment_intent.payment_failed` warning (+ route unit tests: the exact log with and without metadata, no service called, 200).
- [ ] **56.9: Out-of-Order `account.updated` Events** — *unscoped, small.*
  - `syncArtistConnectAccountStatus` writes whichever event arrives last, but Stripe doesn't guarantee delivery order. A delayed older event can overwrite fresh `chargesEnabled`/`payoutsEnabled` values.
  - A stale `true` makes `createDepositPaymentIntent` send `on_behalf_of` to an account that can't take charges, so the deposit can't be created. A stale `false` sends the deposit to the platform instead of the artist.
  - Fix: retrieve the account from Stripe in the handler and write its current values, or skip events older than a stored `event.created`.
- [ ] **56.10: Cancel Allowlist on the Server** — *unscoped, small.*
  - `cancelBookingRequest` blocks only `CANCELLED_BY_CLIENT`, `DECLINED` and `COMPLETED` (`cancelBookingRequest.ts:14`). The UI uses an allowlist instead (`ClientBookingActions.tsx:45-49`), so `NO_SHOW` and `CANCELLED_BY_ARTIST` are blocked only in the browser.
  - A client who calls `cancelBookingRequestAction` directly on their own `NO_SHOW` booking rewrites it to `CANCELLED_BY_CLIENT`, erasing the no-show record, and `refundDeposit` (which has no status check) refunds the deposit that a no-show forfeits (CLAUDE.md 7.3).
  - `cancelBookingRequest.test.ts` has no case for either status.
  - Fix: allow only `PENDING`, `AWAITING_SLOT_CONFIRMATION` and `APPROVED`, from one constant in booking shared by the service and the UI so they can't drift. Add unit tests for `NO_SHOW` and `CANCELLED_BY_ARTIST`. Decide whether `refundDeposit`'s callers should also refuse a non-cancelled status.
  - Same family as 56.2 (handlers that don't check booking status): design them together, ship them separately.
- [ ] **56.11: Failed Refund Recovery** — *unscoped.* Waits for 56.12.
  - After 56.6, a `FAILED` refund only raises a critical alert, and the client sees "Contact support". Stripe returns the money to the platform balance.
  - A new card refund to the same closed card would fail again, so recovery needs another method (bank transfer, credit).
  - Proposed (2026-10-11):
    - Show Stripe's `failure_reason` as plain copy to whoever acts. Check each code against Stripe's docs first: a low platform balance usually holds a refund `pending` (`pending_reason: insufficient_funds`) rather than failing it.
    - Add an inline callout with the next steps.
    - Add a guarded "Mark as refunded another way" action. It sets a new terminal status, `REFUNDED_MANUALLY`, above `FAILED` in 56.6's precedence. Only this action reaches it, never a webhook. "Refunded" then means `SUCCEEDED` or `REFUNDED_MANUALLY`.
  - Design pass:
    - Who acts, the platform or the artist. 56.12 decides who holds the money after a failed refund, and that settles it.
    - Where it lives. The only roles today are `ARTIST` and `CLIENT`, so it's an in-app admin role or an internal tool (Retool, Refine). A tool reads through a read-only database role and writes only through an app endpoint, so billing's status rules and logging still apply.
    - How much of the failure the person acting should see. "Lost or stolen card" is client detail an artist doesn't need.
- [ ] **56.12: Reverse the Connect Transfer on Deposit Refunds** — *unscoped.*
  - Deposits are destination charges (`on_behalf_of` + `transfer_data.destination` in `createDepositPaymentIntent`). `refundDeposit` calls `refunds.create` without `reverse_transfer: true`.
  - Stripe's documented default then leaves the transfer with the artist and debits the platform balance for the refund. So the platform pays for a Connect-routed refund while the artist keeps the deposit. Untested: 56.1 had no connected account.
  - Design pass:
    - Reverse the transfer in full. Partial reversal only matters with an application fee, and there is none today.
    - Decide what a reversal does when the artist's balance is short.
    - Decide what happens to the reversal when the refund later fails. That decides who acts in 56.11.
    - Prove it in test mode with a connected account (Stripe CLI, like 56.1).
- [ ] **56.13: Card on File for Post-Appointment Penalties** — *unscoped.* Added 2026-10-12 (moved here from the backlog draft).
  - When an artist's deposit is £0, nothing is collected up front, so a no-show can't be penalised.
  - Proposed: for £0-deposit configurations, `createDepositPaymentIntent` creates a Stripe SetupIntent instead, vaulting a payment method that a no-show penalty can be charged to off-session.
  - Design pass: how much the penalty is and who triggers it, how it relates to the existing `enforcePrecharge` 50% precharge (CLAUDE.md constraint 4), consent copy for an off-session charge, and SCA handling when an off-session charge needs authentication.
  - Changes the same code as 56.8–56.12, so it comes after them.
  - Design constraint: no new billing → booking calls. `createDepositPaymentIntent` already calls booking; the SetupIntent path must not add more. Vaulted payment-method state goes in a billing-owned table keyed by `bookingRequestId` (or by client, if the design pass decides cards are per client), not in new `BookingRequest` columns. Each new call adds to the circular dependency Phase 57 (`03-backlog.md`) has to undo.
